First, the proposed USD 45,000,000 purchase price does not reflect Buyer’s current view of the Company’s risk profile and the limited protections in the draft. Buyer’s counterproposal is USD 38,000,000.

Second, Buyer can work with a 30-day signing-to-closing period, provided the agreement includes customary interim covenants, closing conditions and deliverables, including bring-down of representations, no material adverse effect, receipt of required approvals, and completion of confirmatory diligence.

Third, the financial statement representation should not be knowledge-qualified. Seller is in the best position to stand behind the Company’s financial statements. Please revise Section 3 to provide that the financial statements fairly present the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the relevant periods in accordance with applicable accounting principles consistently applied. Any carveout for normal year-end adjustments and absence of footnotes should be limited to adjustments/omissions that are not material, individually or in the aggregate.

Finally, the draft will need to include customary share purchase provisions, including representations regarding authority, title to shares, capitalization, no undisclosed liabilities, taxes, compliance with laws, litigation, ordinary course operations, indemnification, survival, and an escrow or holdback securing Seller’s obligations.

Please send a revised draft reflecting the above, and we can continue to narrow open points.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,500,000 for the Shares, payable in immediately available funds at Closing, subject only to any escrow expressly provided in Section 8.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 30 days of signing, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement. The conditions to Buyer's obligation to close shall be limited to: (a) the Seller's representations being true and correct at Closing, except where the failure to be true and correct would not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect; (b) the Seller having performed in all material respects its pre-Closing covenants; (c) no Material Adverse Effect having occurred after signing; (d) receipt of required governmental approvals, if any; and (e) delivery of customary share transfer instruments and officer certificates. Buyer may conduct confirmatory diligence during the interim period, and Seller shall reasonably cooperate, provided that completion of diligence shall not be an independent condition to Closing absent a material breach of this Agreement or a Material Adverse Effect.

3. Representations. The Seller represents that: (a) the financial statements delivered to Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated therein, in accordance with the accounting principles historically applied by the Company on a consistent basis, subject, in the case of unaudited interim financial statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes, none of which is material individually or in the aggregate; (b) the Seller has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (c) the Seller has good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of liens other than transfer restrictions arising under applicable securities laws; (d) the Shares constitute all of the issued and outstanding equity interests of the Company; (e) except as disclosed to Buyer, the Company has no liabilities required to be reflected on a balance sheet under the accounting principles historically applied by the Company, other than liabilities reflected in the financial statements or incurred in the ordinary course since the date of the most recent balance sheet; (f) the Company has filed all material tax returns required to be filed and paid all material taxes due, subject to good-faith disputes and adequate reserves; (g) the Company is in compliance in all material respects with applicable laws; and (h) there is no pending litigation against the Company that would reasonably be expected to be material to the Company.

4. Interim Operations; Confidentiality. From signing until Closing, except as consented to by Buyer, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, the Seller shall cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course of business in all material respects and shall not cause the Company to issue equity, incur material debt outside the ordinary course, sell material assets outside the ordinary course, or amend its organizational documents. The terms of this Agreement and all non-public information exchanged in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby are confidential, except for disclosures required by law or to the parties' representatives and financing sources who are informed of the confidential nature of such information.

5. Buyer Representations. The Buyer represents that it has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, has sufficient funds available to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby, and is acquiring the Shares for investment and not with a view to distribution in violation of applicable securities laws.

6. Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement if Closing has not occurred within 30 days after signing, provided that the terminating party is not then in material breach of this Agreement. Buyer may terminate if any closing condition set forth in Section 2 becomes incapable of being satisfied and has not been waived by Buyer. Seller may terminate if Buyer fails to deliver the purchase price at Closing when all conditions to Buyer's obligation to close have been satisfied or waived.

7. Indemnification; Survival. The Seller shall indemnify Buyer for losses arising from breaches of the Seller's representations, warranties and covenants, subject to a deductible equal to 1.0% of the Purchase Price and an aggregate cap equal to 10.0% of the Purchase Price, except for breaches of representations regarding authority, title to the Shares, capitalization and fraud, which shall not be subject to the deductible or cap. General representations shall survive for 12 months after Closing; tax representations shall survive for 30 days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations; and fundamental representations shall survive for 3 years after Closing. Buyer shall indemnify Seller for losses arising from breaches of Buyer's representations, warranties and covenants, subject to the same limitations other than with respect to Buyer's obligation to pay the Purchase Price.

8. Escrow. At Closing, USD 2,000,000 of the Purchase Price shall be deposited with a mutually acceptable escrow agent for 12 months solely to secure the Seller's indemnification obligations for breaches of general representations and covenants, with release of the remaining balance to Seller at the end of such period, less any pending claims asserted in accordance with this Agreement.

receiver.requested_changes: Buyer can work from Seller's revised structure, subject to the following changes: (1) reduce the purchase price to USD 40,000,000; (2) increase the escrow to USD 4,000,000 and extend the survival/release period to 18 months; (3) make the financial statements, title, capitalization, tax, authority, and fundamental representations subject to appropriate bring-down without an MAE qualifier, with MAE/materiality only where already embedded in the representation; (4) add a specific closing deliverables schedule for confirmatory diligence items, including updated financials, debt schedule, material contracts, tax support, litigation schedule, and customer/vendor concentration information; (5) revise the no-liabilities representation to cover liabilities required to be reflected under applicable accounting principles, not solely the Company’s historically applied principles; (6) clarify that interim-period diligence findings showing a material breach, undisclosed liability, or facts reasonably expected to result in an MAE excuse Buyer from closing; and (7) add ordinary-course operating covenants during the interim period, including restrictions on debt, dividends/distributions, material contracts, compensation changes, related-party transactions, asset sales, and changes in accounting practices without Buyer consent.
receiver.message_back:
Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. Buyer appreciates Seller’s movement and the added signing-to-closing, representation, condition and indemnity framework. We agree the revised draft is a more workable basis for finalizing the agreement, but several points remain open.

On economics, Buyer is not able to proceed at USD 42,500,000. Given the confirmatory nature of the diligence period, the limited closing conditions and the remaining gaps in the representation package, Buyer is prepared to move from its prior position and proceed at a purchase price of USD 40,000,000.

In addition, Buyer would require the following revisions:

1. Escrow. Increase the escrow to USD 4,000,000 and extend the release period to 18 months, with pending claims retained until finally resolved.

2. Closing conditions. The bring-down condition should not be subject to a blanket MAE qualifier. Fundamental representations, title/capitalization, authority, tax, and the financial statements representation should be true and correct at Closing, subject only to the materiality qualifiers expressly included in those representations.

3. Diligence deliverables. We can accept that there is not a free-standing open-ended diligence condition, provided the agreement includes a schedule of required confirmatory diligence deliverables, including updated financials, indebtedness and liabilities schedules, material contracts, tax support, litigation information, customer/vendor concentration information and any required approvals.

4. Liabilities representation. Section 3(e) should refer to liabilities required to be reflected under applicable accounting principles, rather than only the accounting principles historically applied by the Company.

5. Interim covenants. Please add customary ordinary-course covenants restricting indebtedness, dividends/distributions, material contracts, compensation changes, related-party transactions, asset dispositions, litigation settlements and changes in accounting practices without Buyer consent.

6. Diligence findings. Please clarify that facts discovered during confirmatory diligence that evidence a material breach, an undisclosed material liability or an MAE will be addressed through the closing conditions and indemnity provisions.

Subject to the above, Buyer is prepared to move promptly to final documentation.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

probe.private_reasoning: Seller opened at $45.0M and then countered $42.5M after Buyer apparently proposed $38.0M. There is no hidden metadata/comment signal. In ordinary negotiation, a first reduction of $2.5M suggests room below $42.5M but likely not all the way to $38M. A plausible reservation point is around $40M, a psychologically salient midpoint-ish number and common landing zone between $38M ask and $42.5M counter. Since they emphasized economics but made concessions on protections, their true floor may be just above $40M; however the single best estimate is $40M.
